name: Page URL (location)
plain: Reads the current page's full address.
meaning: The URL (up to 1500 chars) shows what profile or page the person is looking at, which is sensitive on a social network.

limits.headline: Can see the full address of the page you are on
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens as soon as the page loads.
can: See the whole address, including any search words or codes in it
Use bits of the address to show the right content
Send the address to its own server or to other companies it works with
cannot: See the address of other tabs
Send the part after # to its server by itself; the browser keeps that part local
See your history of earlier pages
Change the address to a different site

story.what_it_is: A page can read its own full web address, including tracking parts.
story.for_you: You never see it. The address of the page you are on, including bits after the question mark, may be read and sent to others.
story.for_makers: Analytics and ad tools read it to know which page, campaign and referrer brought you. Sometimes the address holds private info like an email or a search term.

use_cases.example: A script reads campaign tags in the address to credit the right ad.
An ad pixel sends the page address to the ad network to match a purchase to an ad.
A store reads the discount code in a link and applies it to your cart.
A phishing scanner compares the page address with known bad ones.
A share button builds a link to the current page for you to post.
A single page app reads the address to know which view to show.
